title: Stop at red lights
summary: Switch the lights on, make running a red cost something and make waiting pay.

steps.title: Switch the lights on
steps.body:
So far the streets were empty and the lights were off. The `each generation` block at the bottom runs once between generations and can change what the next one drives.

Call `useLevel(level: 2)` there. Level 2 is the first with traffic lights. The preview and the test drive follow the level your script asks for, so watch the test driver wait at a red light.

check.message: Call useLevel(level: 2) in the each generation block.

hints: The call goes inside each generation, in place of the comment.

steps.title: A cost for red
steps.body:
`rules.ranRedLight` is true on the tick the SUV enters a junction on red. Running a red light is dangerous, so it should cost points.

Take 2 points away when it happens. A minus sign in front of the number makes a reward a cost.

check.message: Add a reward inside each tick that uses rules.ranRedLight.

hints: A cost is a reward with a minus sign: reward -points when condition.

steps.title: End the trip at a red light
steps.body:
A cost on its own is easy to outweigh. A brain that runs every red gets further along the route and still scores well.

Ending the trip there takes away all the progress it would have made after, which is a lesson every brain learns fast. Add a stop rule for `rules.ranRedLight`.

check.message: Add a stop rule that uses rules.ranRedLight.

hints: Stop rules look like stop "reason" when condition.

steps.title: Make waiting pay
steps.body:
Waiting at a red earns nothing, while driving on earns progress. Until a brain has learned that running reds ends its trip, waiting looks like the worse choice.

A tiny reward for standing at a red light close to its line makes braking pay at once. `light.red` is true while the next light is red, and `light.distance` is how far its stop line is. `light.waited` counts the seconds stood there. Stop paying after 25 s, about one red, or brains learn to sit through cycle after cycle instead of driving on. The built-in reward leaves this pay out: at rush hour even one red per light was worth more to timid brains than crossing the crowds.

The test driver waits at a red on this trip, so its score should pass 18.

check.message: The test drive should score more than 18 points while it waits at the red light.

hints: Combine four conditions with and: the light is red, it is close, the SUV has stopped, and it has waited less than 25 s.
Write reward +0.005 when light.red and light.distance < 25 m and car.speed < 1 m/s and light.waited < 25 s.
